reflection: Which clues depend on daylight? Which depend on local weather or plants?
title: Seasons Explorer
description: Sort twelve seasonal observations in an Alberta nature notebook.
brief: Think about typical seasons in Alberta. Nature’s timing can vary from place to place and year to year.

items.label: New buds opening

items.label: First spring growth

items.label: Longest days of the year
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="21" fill="#edc974"/><path d="M50 6v10M50 84v10M6 50h10M84 50h10M19 19l8 8M73 73l8 8M19 81l8-8M73 27l8-8" stroke="#dba653" stroke-width="4"/></svg>

items.label: Garden growing strongly

items.label: Usually the warmest season

items.label: Days shorten toward winter

items.label: Bare deciduous branches

items.label: Shortest days of the year
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="16" y="19" width="68" height="66" rx="5" fill="#f8eacd"/><path d="M16 39h68M32 12v16M68 12v16"/><path d="M31 52h5M48 52h5M65 52h5M31 68h5M48 68h5M65 68h5" stroke="#bb9ba8" stroke-width="6"/></svg>
items.why: The shortest daylight occurs around the December solstice in the Northern Hemisphere.

notes:
Focus: describe typical seasonal changes in Alberta. These are observations, not rules for every place or every year. Snow can fall outside winter, and plants vary in when they grow or flower.

Earth’s tilted axis causes the yearly pattern of seasons and daylight. It is not caused by Earth being nearer to the Sun in summer.

Content reference: National Weather Service — Why Do We Have Seasons?.
